TGR.basis: Tigrayan provincial lordship, highland agriculture, textiles/craft and armed retainers. University Hist.102 p107; northern regional core compared with Bahru p17 and Haberland. Not a modern ethnic-region boundary.

GJM.basis: Gojjam lordship within the Blue Nile loop, provincial grain/cattle economy, craft and military retinue. Hist.102 pp107,117; regional approximation from river/locality comparison.

WLO.basis: Wollo and adjoining Lasta chiefly networks; cereal/pastoral economy, craft, negotiation and retainers. Aggregate autonomy, not the later Yejju hegemony founded in 1786.

SHW.basis: Ankober/Menz/Yifat Shewan dynastic core under Asfa Wosen from 1775; Hist.102 p92. Excludes nineteenth-century expansion and the future Addis Ababa metropolis.

KFA.basis: Independent Kaffa court in the southwest, agricultural/textile/craft and exchange capability; Haberland pp802-805. Bonga core only, not modern Kaffa administrative province.

WLT.basis: Wolayta kingship attested before the eighteenth century, agrarian production and royal retainers; Haberland pp804-805. Oral dynastic legends do not certify each frontier.

AWS.basis: Awsa lower-Awash oasis polity, Afar court, agriculture/pastoralism, exchange and armed retainers; Haberland p789 and Hist.102. Not direct sovereignty over every Afar coastal sultanate.

HAR.basis: Independent Harar emirate and surrounding local authority, agriculture/crafts/textiles, caravan exchange and armed service; Hist.102 p92. Native Amhara culture is a catalogue proxy, not an ethnic claim.

YJR.basis: Janjero/Yem court between Gibe and Omo systems, established before 1776; Haberland p805. Two-province core and native Sidama proxy, not full modern district or dynastic reconstruction.

HRI.basis: Hiraab imamate/confederate authority and Mogadishu/central coast after Ajuran fragmentation; Kluijver thesis ch2 and Cassanelli ch4. Confederation, not homogeneous central administration.

WLG.basis: Wallaga/Macha Oromo communities under Gadaa and local authorities before the nineteenth-century Leqa monarchies. Hist.102 pp114-116 and Mohammed Hassen SOAS thesis.

ARS.basis: Arsi and adjacent Oromo Gadaa communities east of the Rift; not a nineteenth-century monarchical state. Haberland regional narrative and Hist.102.

BRN.basis: Borana pastoral and Gadaa communities in the south, outside Gondarine direct government. Native tag, not a unitary sultanate.

OMO.basis: Plural southern/Omo communities outside reviewed royal cores. Native aggregate does not claim a single monarchy or ethnic homogeneity; Haberland pp802-805.

BJA.basis: Beja/Bilen/Habab western lowlands, local authorities distinct from Asmara highlands and Ottoman harbours. Aggregate native tag; not a unified Beja kingdom.

OGD.basis: Interior Somali pastoral communities outside Ethiopian direct authority; not a modern national boundary or ethnically uniform cadastral partition.

AFR.basis: Plural Afar coastal and desert authorities outside Awsa royal core; maritime contacts and the inherited coastal anchorage. Ottoman claims do not establish direct highland administration.

HDY.basis: Autonomous Hadiya/Kambata highland communities, Hist.102 pp113-114; a plural local envelope, not revival of the vast medieval Hadiya kingdom.
